ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says the disbelievers are 'waiting for their Lord'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase from Surah Al-Qiyamah is often interpreted as describing the intense, fixed gaze of the disbelievers upon Allah, reflecting a state of stunned anticipation rather than peaceful contemplation. Scholars note that this 'looking' signifies their helplessness and the immediacy of their reckoning, contrasting with the hopeful gaze of the believers. This verse underscores the concept of *Nazar* (gazing) as a physical and spiritual manifestation of one's ultimate fate.
